After active trade policy actions in the first half of April, the second half of the month was relatively quiet. The most significant event was the announcement of a 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs for most countries, which was not extended to China. This pause was seen as a potential opportunity for negotiations, but it did not lead to any significant breakthroughs in US-China trade relations. The US also announced the closure of the de minimis exemption for low-value imports from China and Hong Kong, effective May 2, 2025. This move was aimed at combating China's role in America's synthetic opioid crisis and was part of a broader strategy to tighten trade restrictions on China. China's response during this period included an immediate retaliatory tariff increase to 84% on US goods and a comprehensive diplomatic offensive through the release of a White Paper outlining its position on the trade dispute. Despite these developments, the overall trajectory of US-China trade relations remained fraught with tension and uncertainty.
